Chapter 3: Practicing Spiritual Disciplines for Lasting Change
Now that you’ve started to build trust and become more aware of God’s love, the next step in your journey is all about putting that faith into action—through spiritual disciplines.
But don’t think of these as just religious chores you have to check off. Instead, imagine them as tried-and-true habits that open up space for real transformation.
Think about it like this: when an athlete wants to get better, they train specific muscles. In the same way, spiritual disciplines are how you strengthen your inner life.
Let’s look at some of the core disciplines—and how they can shape your everyday experience.
There’s prayer. And this isn’t just talking at God—it’s also about listening. It’s a real, two-way conversation that helps you build intimacy.
Then you have scripture meditation. That means going beyond just reading a passage. It’s about letting those words soak in, so they actually start shaping how you think and what you do.
Worship is another key part—both on your own and with others. It stirs up gratitude and awe, and it reorients your heart.
What about fasting? That’s when you set aside certain comforts, even just for a while, so you can focus more on what really matters.
And service—using your time and resources to help others. This one’s powerful, because it shifts your focus from yourself to your community.
Each of these disciplines does something unique. Prayer brings you closer, scripture meditation renews your mind, worship lifts your heart, fasting sharpens your focus, and service grows your compassion.
When you bring them all together, you get a balanced approach to growth—kind of like how a good workout routine covers your whole body.
Now, here’s where it gets real: putting these disciplines into practice takes intention. It’s so easy to get distracted, or to feel discouraged when you don’t see instant results. But the secret? Consistency. Just showing up, even if you’re not feeling it.
Over time, these practices turn into habits, and those habits start to shape who you are and how you see the world.
The best way to start is small. Maybe you take a few minutes each morning for prayer, or you read a short passage of scripture before bed. As you get more comfortable, you can go deeper and spend more time.
Remember, the goal isn’t to be perfect—it’s to make progress, one step at a time.
Of course, life gets in the way. You’ll probably run into obstacles like busyness, fatigue, or even doubt. On those days, remind yourself: spiritual disciplines aren’t about trying to earn favor. They’re about making room for God to work in you. Grace is always there, and every day’s a chance to start fresh.
Community can make a huge difference too. When you share your goals with a friend or a group, you get encouragement and accountability. And celebrating those small wins together? That’s what keeps you going.
Over time, the effect is lasting change. Your attitudes shift, your priorities line up with what really matters, and even when life throws challenges your way, you’ll find yourself responding with a steadier faith.
It’s a gradual process—think of it like a tree growing slowly, but strong and steady. And the results? They stick with you for life.
